cards.title: Building a list in a loop
cards.body: Use a `for` loop with `range` to work out a value each round and append it.
cards.code:
tens = []
for i in range(1, 4):
    tens.append(i * 10)
print(tens)

hi.title: Loop mein list banana
hi.body: `range` ke saath `for` loop use karo, har round mein ek value nikaalo aur append karo.

cards.title: One append, one item
cards.body: Each `append` adds exactly one item, so after the loop the list has one item per round.

hi.title: Ek append, ek item
hi.body: Har `append` theek ek item jodta hai, isliye loop ke baad list mein har round ka ek item hota hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print `[10, 20, 30]`, but prints `[30]`. Tap the bug.
cards.code:
tens = []
for i in range(1, 4):
    value = i * 10
tens.append(value)
print(tens)

bug.fix: Line 4 is not indented, so it runs once, after the loop. Indent it to append a value every round.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse `[10, 20, 30]` print karna chahiye, par yeh `[30]` print karta hai. Bug par tap karo.
hi.fix: Line 4 indented nahi hai, isliye woh loop ke baad sirf ek baar chalti hai. Ise indent karo taaki har round mein value append ho.

check.question: What does this print?
check.code:
s = []
for i in range(1, 4):
    s.append(i + i)
print(s)
check.explanation: Each round appends i + i: 2, then 4, then 6.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Har round i + i append karta hai: 2, phir 4, phir 6.

exercise.prompt: Read N, build a list of the squares 1, 4, 9, … up to N × N using `append`, then print it with the numbers separated by spaces.
exercise.promptHi: N padho, `append` se squares 1, 4, 9, … N × N tak ki list banao, phir use spaces se alag numbers ke saath print karo.
exercise.starterCode:
n = int(input())
squares = []
# append the squares of 1 to n
print(" ".join(map(str, squares)))
